title: How Animals Make Sound
description: The academy's animals have gone quiet too. Learn nature's many sound-makers to free their voices.

content.value: Animals make sound the same basic way we do — by vibrating something — but they use a wonderful variety of body parts to do it.

ANIMAL      HOW IT MAKES SOUND
🐦  Birds     vibrate a special voice organ (syrinx)
🦗  Crickets  rub their wings together
🐝  Bees/mosquitoes  vibrate their wings very fast
🐍  Snakes    hiss by pushing air out
🐸  Frogs     vibrate cords in an air sac

The buzz of a bee or the whine of a mosquito isn't a voice at all — it's the sound of their tiny wings beating hundreds of times per second. The faster the wings vibrate, the higher the buzzing sound.
Whether it's a bird's song, a cricket's chirp, or a lion's roar, the rule never changes: some part must VIBRATE to make sound. Nature just found hundreds of clever ways to do it.
A mosquito's annoying whine is faster wing-vibration (higher pitch) than a bee's lower buzz — the pitch tells you how fast the wings are beating!

Key Takeaway: Animals make sound by vibrating different body parts — birds a voice organ, crickets their wings by rubbing, and bees and mosquitoes their fast-beating wings. The rule is always vibration.

quiz.question: The buzzing of a bee is caused by…
quiz.explain: A bee's buzz is the sound of its wings beating rapidly — fast vibration.

quiz.question: Crickets make their chirping sound by…
quiz.explain: Crickets rub their wings together, and the vibration produces the chirp.

quiz.question: What do ALL animal sounds have in common?
options: some part of the animal vibrates
quiz.explain: However they do it, all sound-making animals rely on some part vibrating.
